posts.title: 0.9.2 is up as a beta, with a Linux version for the first time
posts.body: Every book is now also kept as plain files beside your library, with a checkpoint of the whole book every couple of hours, and the new History space lets you search every version a book has kept for a line you cut and read what changed as prose. Character pages are laid out in tabs taken from your own sheet, which is now yours to change, and a long run of fixes keeps your words safe when a connection drops or the same scene is open in two windows. It is a beta for now, so you take it from the release page, and once it has had more testing it becomes the next update that arrives inside the app.

posts.title: There is a newsletter now, if you want the longer version
posts.body: It covers writing and the building of Inkgrove at more length than a release note allows, and since it is only just beginning you would be reading from the first one.

posts.title: Videos about the craft, and about building this in the open
posts.body: There is a channel where I talk through writing and through what goes into Inkgrove, including the parts of drafting that tend to catch people out.
